A room has length 15 feet, width 12 feet and height 10 feet. It has one door of dimensions 8 ft and 3.5 ft, and 2 windows of size 5 ft × 3 ft. Find the cost of painting the four walls and the ceiling at Rs. 50 per ft².
questions.solution:
Given:

Dimension of the room = 15 × 12 × 10 (in feet)

Dimension of the door = 8 × 3.5 (in feet)

Dimension of the window = 5 × 3 (in feet)

Cost of painting = Rs. 50 per ft² 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f193198ca75453b76a6457414a74aaceadc59381aef1114294f48598cd0b96b.png] 

Concept used: 

Total surface area of a cuboid = 2 × (Length × Breadth + Height × Breadth + Length × Height)

Area of a rectangle = Length × Breadth

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d90cd2820fbf2c1a20e27d2330b81ad35742212f22027a383748fe9e4e2d769.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b942214b6692668ce35295dd52789c908d8106e6c4a04bc9f6f2adf20e0942ec.png] 

Surface area of the door = 8 × 3.5 = 28 ft²

Total surface area of the two windows = 2 (5 × 3) = 30 ft²

Surface area of the floor = 15 × 12 = 180 ft²

Surface area of the room excluding the Door, Windows, and Floor = 2 (15 × 12 + 12 × 10 + 15 × 10) - 180 - 28 - 30 = 662 ft²

Hence, the cost of painting the four walls and the ceiling = 662 × 50 = Rs. 33100

**∴ The cost of painting the four walls and the ceiling is Rs. 33100.**

questions.question: Sushant, buys goods worth Rs. 8,000. He gets a discount of 10% on that article. After getting the exemption, he pays tax at the rate of 7.5%. Find the amount that he will have to pay for this item received at his residence, if the shopkeeper charges Rs.200 for home delivery. Takes.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price = Rs. 8000

Discount = 10%

Tax = 7.5%

**Formula used:**

SP for Shopkeeper = CP for Sushant = [(100 - D%)/100] × MP

Tax will implied on the cost price after the discount.

**Calculation:**

CP = [(100 - 10)/100] × 8000

⇒ CP = (90 × 8000)/100

⇒ CP = Rs. 7200

Cost price after tax inclusion = 7200 + 7.5% of 7200

⇒ 7200 + 540 = Rs. 7740

Final cost price after delivery charges = 7740 + 200 = Rs. 7940

∴ The shopkeeper pays Rs. 7940.

questions.question: If x ∶ y = 5 ∶ 7, then (6x - y) ∶ (5x + 3y) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given: 

x ∶ y = 5 ∶ 7

Concept used:

Ratio and Proportion

Calculation:

Let the common ratio be P.

Hence, x = 5P and y = 7P

Thus,

(6x - y) ∶ (5x + 3y)

⇒ (6 × 5P - 7P) : (5 × 5P + 3 × 7P)

⇒ 23P : 46P

⇒ 1 : 2

**∴ (6x - y) ∶ (5x + 3y) is 1 : 2.**

questions.question: Shekhar walked a distance at a speed of 8 km/h. He was in a hurry, so on the return journey he travelled in an autorickshaw at a speed of 24 km/h. Find his average speed for the entire journey.
questions.solution:
Given: 

Shekhar walked a distance at a speed of 8 km/h. 

While returning he travelled in an autorickshaw at a speed of 24 km/h. 

Concept used:

Time × Speed = Distance

Average Speed = {Total Distance over Total Time}

Calculation:

Let the distance covered by the round-trip journey by Shekhar be (D + D) i.e. 2D km.

Time taken while going toward the destination = {D over 8} hours

Time taken while returning back from the destination = {D over 24} hours

Hence, his average speed = {2D over {D over 8} + {D over 24}} = 12 kmph

**∴ His average speed for the entire journey was 12 kmph.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

Let the distance between his starting point and the destination be 24 km.

Time taken while going toward the destination = {24 over 8} hours = 3 hours

Time taken while returning back from the destination = {24 over 24} hours = 1 hour

Hence, his average speed = {24 × 2 over (3 + 1)} = 12 kmph

∴ His average speed for the entire journey was 12 kmph.

questions.question: If a sum increases by 21% after 2 years, then the rate of compound interest per annum, when compounded annually, must be:
questions.solution:
Given:

The sum increases by 21% after 2 years.

Concept used:

Compound interest, CI = P(1 + R/100)n - P

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

N = Time in years

Incremented Value = Initial Value × (1 + Increment%)

Calculation: 

Let the principal amount and rate of interest be Rs. P and R% per annum respectively.

P (1 + R/100)² = P (1 + 21/100)

⇒ P (1 + R/100)2 = P × 1.21

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = 1.21

⇒ (1 + R/100)2 = (1.1)²

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The rate of interest is 10%.**

questions.question: Ratio between average of first four prime numbers and first four composite numbers is
questions.solution:
Concept used: 

Average × Number of entities = Total

Calculation:

First four prime numbers are 2, 3, 5, 7.

First four composite numbers are 4, 6, 8, 9.

Average of the first four prime numbers = (2 + 3 + 5 + 7) ÷ 4 = 4.25

Average of the first four composite numbers = (4 + 6 + 8 + 9) ÷ 4 = 6.75

Ratio = 4.25 : 6.75 = 17 : 27

**∴ Ratio between average of first four prime numbers and first four composite numbers is 17 : 27.**

questions.question: A container has 30 litres of milk, from which 3 litres of milk is taken out and replaced with water. The process is done three times. What is the final ratio of the water and the milk in the container?
questions.solution:
Given:

A container has 30 litres of milk, from which 3 litres of milk is taken out and replaced with water. The process is done three times.

Concept used: 

Mixture and Alligation

Calculation:

The volume of 30L always remains the same throughout the process.

After the first step,

Quantity of Milk = 30 - 3 = 27L

Quantity of water = 3L

Hence, Milk : Water = 27 : 3 = 9 : 1

After the second step,

Quantity of Milk = 27 - 3 × {9 over 10} = 24.3L

Quantity of Water = 3 - 3 × {1 over 10} + 3 = 5.7L

Hence, Milk : Water = 24.3 : 5.7 = 81 : 19

After the third step,

Quantity of Milk = 24.3 - 3 × {81 over 81 + 19} = 21.87L

Quantity of Water = 5.7 - 3 × {19 over 81 + 19} + 3 = 8.13L

Hence, the final ratio of the water to the milk = 8.13 : 21.87 = 271 : 729

∴ The final ratio of the water and the milk in the container is 271 : 729.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**The initial volume of the mixture = 30L which always remains the same throughout the process.

3L i.e 10% of the total mixture is drawn and replaced with water thrice during the process.

Hence, the quantity of milk in the mixture at the end of the process = 30 × 0.9 × 0.9 × 0.9 = 21.87L

Thus, the quantity of water in the mixture at the end of the process = 30 - 21.87 = 8.13L

Hence, the final ratio of the water to the milk = 8.13 : 21.87 = 271 : 729

**∴ The final ratio of the water and the milk in the container is 271 : 729.**

questions.question: Two kinds of rice, the first costing Rs. 65 per kg and the second Rs. 95 per kg, are mixed together. Find the ratio in which the 2 types are mixed so that the mixture costs Rs. 83 per kg.
questions.solution:
Given:

Two kinds of rice, the first costing Rs. 65 per kg and the second Rs. 95 per kg

The mixture costs Rs. 83 per kg

Concept used:

Mixture and Alligation

Calculation:

Let the P kg and Q kg of the first and second type of rice were bought respectively.

Hence,

Price of the first type rice = 65 × P = Rs. 65P

Price of the second type rice = 95 × Q = Rs. 95Q

According to the question,

65P + 95Q = 83 × (P + Q)

⇒ 18P = 12Q

⇒ P : Q = 2 : 3

**∴ The ratio in which the 2 types are mixed so that the mixture costs Rs. 83 per kg is 2 : 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a99f120ac3ec86aca69e4f9d14a5aad9f6a955112899091fc6c35a9d3b81a5e1.png] 

Using the Pivot Technique of Mixture and Alligation,

we can see the distance ratio = 18 : 12 = 3 : 2

Hence, the weight ratio of the first type and second type of rice = 2 : 3

∴ The ratio in which the 2 types are mixed so that the mixture costs Rs. 83 per kg is 2 : 3.

questions.question: During festivals, a banner on a shop displays, 'Pay for 3 and get 5'. The discount percentage offered is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The banner on a shop displays, 'Pay for 3 and get 5'. 

Concept used:

Discount% = {Discount over Cost Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of each item be A.

Hence, the cost price of 5 items = 5A

But, the selling price of the 5 items = 3A

Hence, discount = 5A - 3A = 2A

Thus, discount percentage = {2A over 5A} times 100\% = 40%

∴ The discount percentage is 40%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Getting (5 - 3) = 2 items while paying for only 3.

Hence, discount percentage = {2 over 5} times 100\% = 40%

**∴ The discount percentage is 40%.**

In which years was the average production of the companies, more than 38 lakh metres?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

The average production of the companies on 1996 = (24 + 22 + 40) ÷ 3 = 28.67 lakh

The average production of the companies on 1997 = (29 + 23 + 62) ÷ 3 = 38 lakh

The average production of the companies on 1998 = (34 + 38 + 59) ÷ 3 = 43.67 lakh

The average production of the companies on 1999 = (57 + 49 + 51) ÷ 3 = 52.33 lakh

The average production of the companies on 2000 = (45 + 55 + 52) ÷ 3 = 50.67 lakh

∴ In 1998, 1999, 2000 years the average production of the companies was more than 38 lakh metres.

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of Rs. 15,000 at the end of 5 years is Rs. 9,750. If the rate of interest is 3% lesser, then the interest would be
questions.solution:
Given:

The simple interest on a sum of Rs. 15,000 at the end of 5 years is Rs. 9,750. 

Revised rate of interest is 3% lesser

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the rate of interest be R% per annum

According to the question,

{{15000 times 5 times R} over 100} = 9750

⇒ R = 13%

Hence, revised rate of interest = 13 - 3 = 10%

Thus, interest incurred on Rs. 15000 = {{15000 times 5 times 10} over 100} = Rs. 7500.

**∴ The interest would be Rs. 7500.**
